text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "The sending function in notifications/sms.py is queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage (not send_sms(phone, text)). It takes a household_id plus template/params, checks the household's sms_ok flag (raises ValueError for opted-out households, per tests/test_notifications.py test_opted_out_households_get_no_sms), renders the text from an approved template via render(template_id, params), and appends a SmsMessage to the outbox. SmsMessage (core/models.py:107) has fields id, household_id, phone, template_id, params (dict), text, queued_at, with a to_dict() method — so a resent message CAN carry the same household_id, template_id and params as the original. The message id is built as format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')) using attribute access (sent_messages() returns SmsMessage objects, not dicts). MAX_LENGTH is 140 (asserted in tests/test_notifications.py), not 160. queue_sms also enforces feature('sms_enabled') (RuntimeError if disabled) and the outbox is data/outbox/sms.jsonl (OUTBOX = 'outbox/sms.jsonl'); the gateway records per-id delivery results in data/sms_status.json (STATUS = 'sms_status.json') as {\"SMS-00001\": \"delivered\", ...}, readable via delivery_status() -> dict[str, str] which returns {} if the file does not exist. The outbox is irreversible: nothing ever removes or edits a line, so resends must be new appended records with fresh ids. Note: the copy of notifications/sms.py I could read exposes only send_sms(phone, text, *, now=None) with dict records and MAX_LENGTH=160, which conflicts with the tests and core/models.py; the tests and models (queue_sms, TEMPLATES, render, SmsMessage, MAX_LENGTH==140) are authoritative.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}]}}
